one_line: Poet-composer of the Gita Govinda at the court of Lakshmanasena, weaving song, devotion, and dance in eastern India.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, slender and graceful build, with the lightly toned physique of someone used to reciting, singing, and traveling rather than fighting.
appearance.face: Oval face with a warm medium-brown complexion, fine straight nose, softly defined jaw, expressive almond eyes with long lashes, a small tilak in red on the forehead, and a default serene, slightly smiling expression that brightens when he sings.
appearance.hair: Smooth black hair parted in the middle, drawn back into a low, neat knot at the nape of the neck, with a slim cream-colored cloth band tied around the head like a simple turban-strip, ends tucked by the right ear.
appearance.costume: A long, finely woven off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and around the torso like a shawl, bordered with a narrow maroon stripe; beneath it a knee-length pale cream angavastra-style wrap over the upper body, and a full, ankle-length dhoti in soft turmeric-yellow tied at the waist in the Bengali style with pleats in front; he is barefoot, with a single thin maroon thread anklet on the left ankle, and wears modest jewellery—a simple tulsi bead mala around his neck, small gold stud earrings, and a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist; the fabrics are plain, slightly textured handloom cotton with only subtle striped borders at the edges, avoiding heavy ornamentation but suggesting courtly refinement.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a thin red cord in his left hand, its edges slightly darkened with use, accompanied by a small wooden stylus tucked into his waist sash.

ref_desc: Jayadeva is a slender, mid-30s poet with medium-brown oval face, black hair in a low knot with a cream headband, wearing off-white shawl, cream upper wrap, turmeric-yellow Bengali dhoti, simple beads and bangles, and holding a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus in maroon-cream tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Jayadeva, the 12th-century eastern Indian poet, as a dignified, modestly dressed figure: a slender man in his mid-30s with a medium-brown oval face, expressive almond eyes, a small red tilak on his forehead, and smooth black hair parted in the middle and tied back into a low knot at the nape of his neck, wrapped with a slim cream cloth band like a simple headband; his costume is a historically accurate late-12th-century eastern Indian ensemble with a finely woven off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and around the torso like a shawl, its edges marked by a narrow maroon stripe, over a plain pale cream upper wrap reaching to the knees, and an ankle-length turmeric-yellow dhoti tied in the Bengali style with pleats in front and a soft knot at the waist, all in unpatterned, slightly textured handloom cotton with subtle stripe borders; he is barefoot, with a thin maroon thread anklet on his left ankle, a tulsi bead mala around his neck, small gold stud earrings, and a narrow copper bangle on his right wrist; in his left hand he carries a neatly tied palm-leaf manuscript bundle with its darkened leaf edges visible, while a small wooden stylus is tucked into his waist sash, and the overall color scheme centers on off-white, cream, turmeric-yellow, maroon accents, and soft brown skin tones, shown from multiple angles to emphasize the consistent face, hair, drape of garments, and the manuscript as his constant prop.
